claims.text: PtPdCoCuNi high-entropy alloy nanoparticles can be deposited with uniform dispersion on SiO2.
The initial PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles are a uniform single-phase solid solution.
SiO2 functions as an inert support throughout the proposed thermal and redox cycling.
A pre-oxidation treatment can form a thin, controlled, and stable surface oxide layer on PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles.
The engineered oxide layer can remain intact at its designed thickness during cycling from 473 K to 1923 K under alternating reducing and mildly oxidizing atmospheres.
The surface oxide reduces surface-atom mobility by acting as a physical and chemical diffusion barrier.
Reduced surface-atom mobility suppresses elemental segregation in PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles at high temperature.
The oxide barrier suppresses nanoparticle sintering during high-temperature redox cycling.
Pre-oxidized PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles will retain a homogeneous, single-phase solid-solution structure during cycling better than untreated nanoparticles.
Pre-oxidized PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles will undergo less compositional change than untreated nanoparticles.
Untreated PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles will exhibit phase segregation and compositional inhomogeneity under the proposed cycling conditions.
Pre-oxidized PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles will retain catalytic performance better than untreated nanoparticles.
Pre-oxidized PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles will retain thermoelectric performance better than untreated nanoparticles.
Rapid dissolution or transformation of the oxide under extreme redox swings would weaken or eliminate the predicted stabilization.
The surface oxide may alter the intrinsic catalytic active sites of PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles.
